title: CliME: Evaluating Multimodal Climate Discourse on Social Media and the Climate Alignment Quotient (CAQ)

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating LLM-generated climate discourse using a 'Justice' analytical lens to assess whether the models acknowledge how climate transition costs and systemic inequities disproportionately affect low-income communities.

Applying the 'Justice' lens to check for US-centric focus in LLM outputs, evaluating whether the models neglect the vulnerabilities of Global South nations and fail to address historical accountability for global emissions.

Using the 'Justice' lens to analyze if LLM descriptors center or omit marginalized communities, specifically checking for the inclusion of absent voices like Indigenous groups and the acknowledgment of cultural contexts and historical power imbalances.

Employing a 'Criticality' analytical lens to evaluate whether LLM-generated narratives oversimplify systemic barriers, uncritically frame policies, or reinforce partisan divides regarding climate change.
